Type I DM is an autoimmune disorder. We’re all born with some possibility of developing these kinds of conditions. Many genes are involved, and the more “bad” alleles you carry, the more likely you are to develop one or more of the condition. There also needs to be some sort of environmental stimulus to set off an autoimmune condition. These triggers are generally unidentified.

Type I DM often develops at a young age because the autoimmune destruction of the pancreas generally begins fairly early in life, but symptoms don’t manifest until the relevant portions of the pancreas (Islet beta cells) are almost completely obliterated. At that point, your body lacks insulin, your cells can’t absorb sugar, it gets stuck in your blood, and you get diabetic ketoacidosis like this kid. This is actually a pretty classic initial presentation for type I DM.
